idea-cafe-coffee-250-rupees-owner-margin.angle: Hook: 'Is ₹250 ke cup mein coffee sirf ₹20-25 ki hai, baaki paisa kahan gaya?' Split the cup into ingredient, rent, staff, royalty and profit. Payoff: the owner's real margin, and why rent and footfall matter more than the coffee.
idea-cafe-coffee-250-rupees-owner-margin.hook_pattern: A familiar everyday price broken into slices with a shocking raw-cost figure, like the pizza and Zomato order reels.
idea-cafe-coffee-250-rupees-owner-margin.why_it_works: No scraped reels this week, so this is reasoning. Cafes are a very common dream business for men aged 18 to 34, and the pizza franchise reel already shows that a franchise unit-economics breakdown works. The low raw-material cost against a high menu price makes a curiosity hook that gets shared.

idea-builder-profit-on-1-crore-flat.title: ₹1 Crore Ka Flat Bika: Builder Ke Paas Kitna Bacha?
idea-builder-profit-on-1-crore-flat.topic: Where the ₹1 crore of a new flat goes: land cost, construction, approvals and FSI, GST and stamp duty, marketing and broker fees, finance cost, and builder margin, using listed developers' public margins.
idea-builder-profit-on-1-crore-flat.angle: Hook: 'Aapne ₹1 crore ka flat kharida. Builder ne usme se kitna kamaya?' Show a stacked-bar breakdown by cost bucket. Payoff: the builder's EBITDA or margin range, and how much is land versus tax versus actual construction.
idea-builder-profit-on-1-crore-flat.hook_pattern: Follow ₹X of the customer's money through the chain to the owner's pocket, the same as the gas cylinder and school fee reels.
idea-builder-profit-on-1-crore-flat.why_it_works: No scraped reels this week, so this is reasoning. The home loan reels cover the buyer's side, and this is the seller's side, which people almost never see. Real estate is the most universal aspiration for this audience, and listed developers like DLF and Godrej Properties publish margins, so the numbers are researchable.

idea-airline-ticket-5000-where-money-goe.title: ₹5,000 Ki Flight Ticket: Airline Ko Kitna Bachta Hai?
idea-airline-ticket-5000-where-money-goe.topic: Per-seat economics of an Indian airline: fuel share, aircraft lease, crew, airport and navigation charges, load factor, break-even load factor, ancillary revenue, and why airlines often lose money.
idea-airline-ticket-5000-where-money-goe.angle: Hook: 'Ek flight bhar ke bhi airline ka profit sirf ₹300-400 kyun hota hai?' Slice the fare into fuel, lease, airport fees, taxes and crew. Payoff: break-even seat occupancy, and why bag fees, seat selection and food earn more than the ticket.
idea-airline-ticket-5000-where-money-goe.hook_pattern: Fare vs hidden costs, with a counter-intuitive twist that a full plane still doesn't mean profit (like the sleeper bus and sarkari bus contract reels).
idea-airline-ticket-5000-where-money-goe.why_it_works: No scraped reels this week, so this is reasoning. The sleeper bus and truck reels show the audience cares about transport economics and 'is it full, but still no profit?' twists. Airlines are the ultimate dream-business curiosity, and DGCA and listed airline filings give public numbers.

airline break-even load factor India
airline ancillary revenue share India

idea-railway-platform-stall-licence-econ.title: Railway Station Pe Chai-Snacks Stall: Licence Kaise Milta Hai Aur Kitna Kamate Hain?
idea-railway-platform-stall-licence-econ.topic: How IRCTC/Indian Railways catering stall licences are awarded (tender or bid, licence fee), typical fees for station categories, product price control, staff cost, daily sales, and realistic owner take-home.
idea-railway-platform-stall-licence-econ.angle: Hook: 'Platform pe ₹20 ki chai bechne ka haq kaun deta hai, aur uski licence fee kitni hai?' Explain the licence route, the licence fee as a fixed monthly cost, and the footfall versus sales maths. Payoff: monthly profit at a busy station vs a small one, and the hidden costs.
idea-railway-platform-stall-licence-econ.hook_pattern: Insider access to a licensed, hard-to-enter business ('who actually gets to run this'), like the Amul parlour and gas agency reels.
idea-railway-platform-stall-licence-econ.why_it_works: No scraped reels this week, so this is reasoning. Licence-based businesses (gas agency, Amul parlour, wine shop) fit our best-performing 'dream business, hidden access' angle. Railway stalls are visible to everyone daily but the process is a mystery, and Railways' catering policy documents are public.
